candidate_042_update.name: episodic reflective strategy memory with machine-enforceable diversity and constraint actuator

new_primary_evidence.title: Constraint-Aware Corrective Memory for Language-Based Drug Discovery Agents
new_primary_evidence.observation: On a 30-target LIDDiA drug-design benchmark with the same DeepSeek controller family, unchanged molecular toolchain/action space and a 10-iteration cap, reproduced baseline target success was 73.3% (22/30). Adding a deterministic set-level repair signal without the full structured-memory stack raised it to 86.7% (26/30). Full CACM reached 100% (30/30), with average final pool size 5.0 versus 21.0 and average terminal iteration 3.07 versus 4.40.
new_primary_evidence.ablation_scope: Fixed, known protocol constraints in computational molecular design. This directly supports a machine-legible repair/control signal and selective corrective memory under this benchmark, not arbitrary self-generated reflection constraints or open-ended scientific validity.
new_primary_evidence.causal_boundary: The actuator half now has a matched partial positive control. The bridge from free-form episodic reflection to automatically compiled enforceable diversity/budget/no-repeat constraints remains untested.

matched_repair_search_status.result: Closest partial matched evidence found: CACM holds the DeepSeek controller family, molecular toolchain/action space and iteration cap fixed while adding explicit set-level protocol audit/repair signals and corrective memory. Exact same-model/tools/budget critique-only versus mandatory evidence-changing repair/block for open-ended scientific inference remains unresolved.
matched_repair_search_status.scope_guard: Do not treat fixed protocol satisfaction in drug design as proof of autonomous scientific claim repair or epistemic validity.
